newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ireland fights for satellite fish tracking accord.
newsitem.headline: Ireland fights for satellite fish tracking accord.

text.p: The Irish presidency was holding bilateral talks on Friday with Spain and other countries blocking an agreement to set up a satellite system to monitor fishing vessels, EU officials said.
In a bid to resolve objections to a Commission proposal presented in 1993, Ireland has put forward a compromise to exempt more vessels and delay start-up of the scheme.
Ireland has suggested that only vessels over 24 metres overall length should be tracked by satellites, compared with the Commission proposal of 18 metres.
The start of the first phase, covering fishing in non-EU waters and industrial fishing, would be delayed 18 months to June 30, 1998.
The start of the second phase, covering all EU fishing, would be delayed two years until January 1, 2000.
Vessels at sea for less than 24 hours or operating within the 12-mile limit would be exempted from the scheme.
But Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Sweden and Denmark still had reservations and would form a blocking minority, officials said.
Spain, which has the biggest distant water fleet of large vessels, says the scheme is discriminatory because it would affect 1,000 Spanish vessels, or 25 percent of the total.
Italy, which would have 800 vessels tracked, also said the vessel size limit was discriminatory and demanded that only vessels over 26 metres overall length be included.
The Dutch were also unhappy as 350 of their vessels out of a fleet of some 500 would be affected.
Under the Commission's original proposal, 9,000 vessels would have been tracked by satellite.
The Irish compromise would also allow countries to use cheaper alternative systems, such as automatic position recorders, for reporting vessel movements.
Such systems could be used for vessels fishing in non-sensitive areas for stocks which are not endangered and where data is not urgently required.
